transform.scale_note: RealityCapture units are not metres: upholstered seats (the largest up-facing area below 1 m) are 1.03 units high, taken as 0.45 m; the ceiling is then 5.1 m, close to the 4.9 m dining room on the same floor

colour.method: partial grey-world white balance (strength 0.2) then gamma on sRGB values toward median luminance 0.42 (gamma clamped to [0.75, 1.15])

preview.texture_format: KTX2 ETC1S (basisu -q 255, mipmaps, sRGB), baked on a new UV atlas (xatlas)
preview.simplify: gltfpack -si 0.040000 -se 0.05 on welded positions (from 999999 tris), re-atlased and re-baked

artworks.note: Brussels, second half of the 16th century (catalogue: 1560-1600). Repaired in 1896 by Handarbetets vänner, which wove partly new borders; the museum's record of the trial weaving (https://samlingar.shm.se/object/412BA408-BEED-4F5E-B133-3A837FD1D392) states it repeats the material, technique, pattern and colours of the original border, so the 1896 work copies the 16th-century design.

artworks.label: Interior architecture: gilded panelling, coffered ceiling frame, fireplace, designed by Isak Gustaf Clason (drawing HWY LXIV:III:B.b.b.64)
